forward_geometry_elements.name: discrete_torus_T4
forward_geometry_elements.description: Tau state lives on T^4 = Z/2 x Z/5 x Z/2 x Z/12 (240 points)

forward_geometry_elements.name: operator_state_fiber_bundle
forward_geometry_elements.description: State = (base_angle b, fiber_phase phi, radial_class r, spin_h, tau)
forward_geometry_elements.structure: product: torus x fiber x radial_shells x spin_word x tau_phases

forward_geometry_elements.name: six_geometric_operators
forward_geometry_elements.description: T_b (torus advance), T_x (swap), T_y (twist), T_c (coupled kick), T_z' (fiber lift), T_r* (radial transport)

forward_geometry_elements.name: holonomy_corrections
forward_geometry_elements.description: Transport operators use active_transport_lift_core_v6 with coupled_holonomy_residue_v6 and sigma_family_holonomy_law_v6

forward_geometry_elements.name: hopf_fibration_map
forward_geometry_elements.description: S^3 decomposition into base (chi, delta) and transported fiber phase (alpha_t = alpha + 0.5*lambda*cos(2*chi)*delta)

forward_geometry_elements.name: precomputed_state_tables
forward_geometry_elements.description: 343,665 states enumerated by BFS. TN=(N,6,21) tau-nexts, TR=(N,6) state transitions

forward_geometry_elements.name: D_step_recurrence
forward_geometry_elements.description: 24-step sequential trajectory on state space with Gumbel-softmax operator routing

training_rule_elements.name: loss_function
training_rule_elements.description: Cross-entropy on x0 prediction, no geometric structure

training_rule_elements.name: gradient_computation
training_rule_elements.description: torch.autograd reverse-mode through 24-step recurrence, Euclidean Jacobians at each step

training_rule_elements.name: optimizer
training_rule_elements.description: SGD with flat Euclidean metric, lr=0.02, identity preconditioner

training_rule_elements.name: gradient_clipping
training_rule_elements.description: clip_grad_norm with max_norm=1.0, Euclidean L2 norm

training_rule_elements.name: tau_representation
training_rule_elements.description: One-hot encoding of T^4 phases in R^21, destroying cyclic adjacency

mismatch_points.name: one_hot_destroys_cyclic_adjacency
mismatch_points.description: One-hot encoding maps adjacent cyclic phases to orthogonal vectors (distance sqrt(2)). Gradients see no connection between lift_phase=11 and lift_phase=0 despite being one step apart on Z/12.

mismatch_points.name: soft_mixture_in_wrong_space
mismatch_points.description: Euclidean convex combination of one-hot tau vectors produces interior points with no geometric meaning on T^4. Angular circular mean would be the natural operation.

mismatch_points.name: sgd_flat_metric_ignores_torus_curvature
mismatch_points.description: SGD uses identity metric on parameter space. Loss surface inherits anisotropy from torus structure: different phase blocks (mod 2 vs mod 12) may have very different effective curvature.

mismatch_points.name: euclidean_adjoint_not_geometric_adjoint
mismatch_points.description: Backward pass computes Euclidean Jacobian chain through 24 steps, not the geometric adjoint of the transport. Forward operators use holonomy corrections; backward has no corresponding connection term.

mismatch_points.name: no_transport_nontransport_gradient_distinction
mismatch_points.description: Transport operators (T_c, T_z', T_r*) implement geometrically distinct operations from non-transport (T_b, T_x, T_y), but gradient treats all 6 operator weight dimensions identically.

mismatch_points.name: full_fiber_bundle_riemannian_structure
mismatch_points.description: The operator algebra may implement a discrete connection on a fiber bundle. If so, the correct optimizer would use the connection-induced Riemannian metric.

proven_claims: Tau state space is T^4 = Z/2 x Z/5 x Z/2 x Z/12 (discrete torus, 240 points)
One-hot encoding destroys cyclic adjacency (all distinct phases equidistant at sqrt(2))
Training rule is flat Euclidean SGD with no manifold awareness
Soft tau mixture operates in ambient R^21 via Euclidean convex combination
Forward operators implement explicit geometric transformations with holonomy corrections
Paper establishes Hopf fibration captures angular structure; mechanism is primarily fiber-phase-based (alpha = +20.6pp, transport = +2pp more)
The D-step recurrence is mathematically sequential (nonlinear coupled recurrence)
plausible_claims: Angular encoding of tau phases would improve learning by respecting cyclic adjacency
SGD's flat metric is a material bottleneck for this loss surface geometry
Euclidean backward pass produces materially different credit assignment than geometric backward
Transport operators would benefit from different gradient treatment than non-transport operators
Smaller angular representation (8 dims vs 21) may also speed up the sequential recurrence
speculative_claims: The full operator algebra state space has smooth manifold structure
A full Riemannian optimizer would provide large gains beyond angular encoding
Holonomy corrections in operators correspond to curvature that materially affects the loss landscape
The fiber bundle interpretation extends from the Hopf routing (paper) to the full operator algebra (implementation)

recommended_next_experiment.name: angular_phase_encoding_vs_onehot
recommended_next_experiment.description: Replace one-hot tau encoding (21 dims) with angular cos/sin pairs (8 dims). Each cyclic phase k in Z/m becomes (cos(2*pi*k/m), sin(2*pi*k/m)). Rebuild TN/tau0 tables with angular encoding. Compare convergence speed, final accuracy, and gradient behavior against one-hot baseline on the same task.
what_stays_same: Attention pooling with pos0 bias fix
SGD with lr=0.02, same temperature schedule, same gradient clipping
measurements: Convergence speed (loss curve over training steps)
Gradient norms per parameter group over training
Wall-time per step (angular model has smaller matrices)
recommended_next_experiment.positive_result_meaning: One-hot encoding was fighting the torus geometry. Training rule credit assignment was misaligned due to coordinate system choice.
recommended_next_experiment.negative_result_meaning: MLP is powerful enough to learn cyclic structure from one-hot data, or one-hot provides useful information for attention pooling. Redirects investigation to C.3/C.4 mismatches.
followup_if_positive: Angular auxiliary loss (regularize soft tau toward valid angular states)
Phase-aware preconditioner (block-diagonal, separate rates for angular vs embedding)
Circular weighted mean for soft mixture (replace Euclidean average with circular mean per phase pair)
